title: Scaling Ratios: The 5-Step Warp Routine
subtitle: Ratios · Mission 02
tagline: Scale a ratio {{cyan:up}} or {{amber:down}} without wrecking the recipe — in five clean steps.

slides.headline: Space Command just radioed in: {{cyan:7 Alien Cadets}} need {{amber:5 Fuel Crystals}}. But {{cyan:28 cadets}} just boarded. How many crystals now?
body: You already know you can't just add more crystals and hope. The recipe is `7 to 5` — mess with that, and the fleet runs out of fuel halfway to the next waystation.
The move: `scale` the ratio. Multiply (or divide) both sides by the same number — the `scale factor` — and the recipe stays balanced no matter how big the mission gets.

Today's power-up: a **5-step warp routine** you can run on any ratio, any mission, any time. By the end of this briefing you'll solve the 28-cadet problem yourself — and Space Command gets its answer. 🚀

slides.definition: The `scale factor` is the number you {{cyan:multiply or divide both parts}} of a ratio by to grow or shrink it — without changing the recipe.
slides.plainWords: It's the warp multiplier. Whatever you do to one side, you do to the other.
slides.analogy: Think of it like **doubling a recipe**. If 1 batch of cookies needs 2 cups flour and 1 cup sugar, a scale factor of 3 means 6 cups flour and 3 cups sugar. Same cookies — just more of them.

slides.definition: A `waystation` is a {{cyan:stopover at 1}} — the `unit rate`. When direct scaling isn't a clean whole number, you dock at 1 first, then warp up to the target.
slides.plainWords: If you can't jump straight from 3 to 10, scale down to 1 first, then scale up to 10.
slides.analogy: Think of it like a **layover flight**. No direct route from Chicago to Tokyo today? Fly through LA. Takes an extra step, but you still land on time. 🛰️

slides.headline: A ratio can scale **up** or scale **down**. Same rules, opposite move.
slides.intro: Every ratio is a pair of `cargo bays` of equal size. When you scale, you add or remove bays — but each bay stays the same inside.

cards.name: SCALE UP (×)
cards.description: You need a {{cyan:bigger fleet}}. **Multiply** both parts of the ratio by the same whole number. Add identical cargo pods to the fleet.

example.label: EXAMPLE
example.text: `3 : 2` scaled up by ×4 becomes `12 : 8`. Four times the cadets, four times the crystals. Recipe stays `3 to 2`.

cards.name: SCALE DOWN (÷)
cards.description: You need a {{amber:smaller scout team}}. **Divide** both parts by the same whole number. Beam alien groups out of the cargo bays, keeping each bay the same size.

example.label: EXAMPLE
example.text: `20 : 15` scaled down by ÷5 becomes `4 : 3`. Smaller crew, same recipe.

slides.headline: Run these five steps — in order — on every scaling mission. 🧮
slides.intro: Lock this routine in. Every single ratio-scaling problem you'll ever hit yields to this exact sequence.

rows.name: Step 1 — Locate the Base Command Pair
rows.description: Find the row where **both** numbers are known. That's your baseline recipe. Example: `7 Cadets : 5 Crystals`.

counter.label: COMMON TRAP
counter.text: Don't grab the row with the unknown. The base pair is the one that's fully logged.

rows.name: Step 2 — Identify the Target Mission Row
rows.description: Find the row with the {{amber:unknown}} you need to solve for. Example: `12 Cadets : ? Crystals`.

rows.name: Step 3 — Calculate the Warp Scale Factor
rows.description: Ask: *what do I multiply (or divide) the known side of the base pair by to reach the target?* Example: `4 × ? = 12` → scale factor is **3**.

counter.label: DIRECTION CHECK
counter.text: Target is bigger → multiply (scale up). Target is smaller → divide (scale down).

rows.name: Step 4 — Apply the Same Fleet Operation
rows.description: Do the **exact same thing** to the other side. If you multiplied cadets by 3, multiply crystals by 3. `3 × 3 = 9 Crystals`.

rows.name: Step 5 — Log and Verify
rows.description: Write the answer in. Then {{cyan:check}}: does your new ratio simplify back to the base pair? `12 : 9` ÷ 3 = `4 : 3`. ✓ Fleet balanced.

slides.headline: Say it out loud. These `sentence stems` turn the math into language you can share with your Math Navigator.
slides.intro: Use these when you're working with a partner, explaining to a teacher, or thinking through a tricky problem on your own.

cards.name: THE RECIPE STEM
cards.description: Use this to **name the base ratio** before you touch any numbers.

example.label: SAY
example.text: *"For every ___ Alien Cadets, Space Command requires ___ Fuel Crystals."*

cards.name: THE BALANCE STEM
cards.description: Use this to **justify your move** after you apply the scale factor.

example.label: SAY
example.text: *"Because I scaled the Cadets up/down by multiplying/dividing by ___, I must scale the Crystals by ___ to maintain orbital equilibrium."*

prompt.label: SUPPORTED SOLVE
prompt.scenario: Base pair: `2 Alien Cadets : 3 Fuel Crystals`. Target: `10 Alien Cadets : ? Crystals`. Walk the 5 steps.
prompt.question: Fill in each blank to run the warp routine.

slides.template: Scale factor: 2 × {{1}} = 10.  Apply to crystals: 3 × {{2}} = {{3}} Crystals.  Verify: 10 : {{3}} ÷ {{1}} = 2 : 3. ✓

blanks.hint: Same scale factor as cadets. Both sides, same move.

hint.altText: Step 3 of the warp routine: compare base to target to find the scale factor.

correct.title: ✓ FLEET BALANCED
body: You ran all five steps clean. Scale factor **5**, applied to both sides, verified back to `2 : 3`.
**Pro move:** Any time you solve a scaling problem, write the scale factor *first* and circle it. Everything else flows from that one number.
correct.followup: Say it with the stem: *"For every 2 cadets, Space Command requires 3 crystals."*

wrongDefault.title: ✕ RECALIBRATE
body: Close — check your scale factor first. **2 × ? = 10.** Lock that number in, then apply the same number to the crystals.
Remember: whatever you do to one side, you do to the other.

prompt.label: SEQUENCE CHECK
prompt.question: Put the 5 steps of the warp routine in the correct order.

items.text: Log and verify: does the new ratio simplify back to the base pair?
Locate the Base Command Pair (the row where both numbers are known).
Apply the same scale factor to the other side of the ratio.
Identify the Target Mission Row (the row with the unknown).
Calculate the Warp Scale Factor: known base × ? = known target.

correct.title: ✓ ROUTINE LOCKED IN
body: Locate → Identify → Calculate → Apply → Verify. That's the whole mission.
**Memory trick:** *Little Imps Can't Avoid Verification.* Dumb mnemonic. It works.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ ORDER'S OFF
body: Think about it this way: you can't calculate a scale factor until you know the base pair AND the target. And you can't verify until you've applied.
Locate first. Identify second. Then math.

prompt.label: APPLIED SOLVE
prompt.scenario: Base pair: `4 Cadets : 5 Crystals`. Target: `20 Cadets : ? Crystals`.
prompt.question: Find the scale factor and the missing number. Two blanks only.

correct.title: ✓ SCALED UP
body: Scale factor **5**, applied cleanly. `20 : 25` ÷ 5 = `4 : 5`. ✓
**Pro move:** Notice you didn't need every step written out this time. Once the routine is in your head, you can run it fast.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ CHECK THE SCALE FACTOR
body: Start over at Step 3. What number times 4 equals 20? That's your scale factor. Then multiply 5 by that same number.

prompt.label: SMALLER CREW
prompt.scenario: Base pair logged in the mission log: `20 Cadets : 24 Fuel Crystals`. The commander only needs a scout team of `5 Cadets`.
prompt.question: How many Fuel Crystals does the scout team need?

correct.title: ✓ CLEAN SCALE-DOWN
body: Scale factor: `20 ÷ 4 = 5`, so you divided by **4**. Then `24 ÷ 4 = 6 Crystals`. ✓
**Pro move:** When the target is *smaller* than the base, you're dividing. The direction tells you the operation.

a.title: ✕ CLOSE — BUT CHECK THE OPERATION
body: **9 Crystals** would happen if you *subtracted* 15 from 24. But scaling isn't subtraction — it's division (when going down) or multiplication (when going up).
Scale factor: `20 ÷ 4 = 5`, so divide crystals: `24 ÷ 4 = 6`.

c.title: ✕ RIGHT MOVE, WRONG NUMBER
body: You divided — good instinct — but **4** is `24 ÷ 6`, not `24 ÷ 4`.
Scale factor comes from the cadets: `20 ÷ 5 = 4`. Then crystals: `24 ÷ 4 = 6`.

d.title: ✕ MISFIRE — THAT'S SUBTRACTION
body: **19 Crystals** = `24 − 5`. That's a subtraction move. Scaling multiplies or divides, it never subtracts.
Scale factor is 4 (down). `24 ÷ 4 = 6 Crystals`.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ RECALIBRATE
body: Base pair: `20 : 24`. Target: `5 : ?`. Scale factor: `20 ÷ ? = 5`, so you're dividing by **4**. Apply to crystals: `24 ÷ 4 = 6`.

prompt.label: DOCK AT 1 FIRST
prompt.scenario: Base pair: `3 Cadets : 12 Crystals`. Target: `? Crystals for 7 Cadets`. There's no clean whole number scale factor from 3 to 7 — so dock at the `waystation` first.
prompt.question: Fill in the waystation route.

slides.template: Step A — Dock at 1 Cadet. 12 ÷ 3 = {{1}} Crystals per Cadet (unit rate).  Step B — Warp up: {{1}} × 7 = {{2}} Crystals.

blanks.hint: Divide crystals by cadets to get crystals per 1 cadet.
Multiply the unit rate by the number of cadets you actually need.

hint.altText: Dock at the unit rate (1 cadet) first, then multiply up to the target number of cadets.

correct.title: ✓ WAYSTATION ROUTE COMPLETE
body: Unit rate is **4 Crystals per Cadet**. Multiply by 7 cadets → **28 Crystals**. Scenic route, same destination.
**Pro move:** The waystation (unit rate) always works, even when the direct scale factor is clean. If you ever get stuck, dock at 1.
correct.followup: Say it with the stem: *"For every 1 Cadet, Space Command requires 4 Crystals."*

wrongDefault.title: ✕ RECALIBRATE AT THE WAYSTATION
body: First get to **1 Cadet**: `12 ÷ 3 = 4 Crystals per Cadet`. That's your unit rate.
Then warp up: `4 × 7 = 28 Crystals`.

slides.tag: ⚡ TACTICAL DRILL · CFU 06 · BIG IDEA CHECK

prompt.label: WHY DOES IT WORK?
prompt.question: Why do you have to multiply (or divide) **both** parts of the ratio by the same scale factor?

options.text: Because it's a math rule teachers made up.
Because the two parts have to stay in the same recipe — if you change one and not the other, the ratio becomes a different recipe.
Because big numbers are harder than small numbers.
Because scale factors only work on even numbers.

correct.title: ✓ YOU GET IT
body: A ratio is a *comparison*. If you change one side but not the other, you've changed what you're comparing — and the recipe is gone.
**Pro move:** This is why the balance stem matters: *"Because I scaled Cadets by ___, I must scale Crystals by ___ to maintain orbital equilibrium."* The 'must' is doing real work in that sentence.

a.title: ✕ IT'S NOT ARBITRARY
body: Math rules aren't invented — they're how the comparison stays true. If you double only the cadets but not the crystals, you've changed the recipe. The crystals-per-cadet amount is different now.
The correct answer: both sides stay in the same recipe.

c.title: ✕ NOT ABOUT SIZE
body: Big numbers aren't the issue. A ratio of `2 : 3` works the same whether you scale it to `20 : 30` or `200 : 300`. The point is keeping *both* parts in balance.

d.title: ✕ NO — ANY WHOLE NUMBER WORKS
body: Scale factors work with any whole number: 2, 3, 5, 7, whatever. The reason you scale both sides is to keep the recipe intact.

wrongDefault.title: ✕ THINK RECIPE
body: Picture doubling a cookie recipe. If you double the flour but keep the sugar the same, you've made a *different* cookie. Same with ratios: both parts, same move.

prompt.label: CLOSE THE LOOP
prompt.scenario: Remember the 28 Alien Cadets that boarded at the start of your shift? Space Command is still on the comms, waiting. Base pair: `7 Cadets : 5 Crystals`. Target: `28 Cadets : ? Crystals`. Run the warp routine.
prompt.question: How many Fuel Crystals does Space Command need for 28 Alien Cadets?

correct.title: ✓ FLEET FUELED · MISSION CLOSED
body: Scale factor **4** (because `7 × 4 = 28`). Apply it: `5 × 4 = 20 Crystals`. Space Command confirms receipt — the fleet eats tonight.
**Pro move:** You just ran the whole warp routine on the problem that opened this mission. That's the entire skill — the recipe stays true no matter how big the fleet gets.
correct.followup: Say it with the balance stem: *"Because I scaled the Cadets up by multiplying by 4, I must scale the Crystals by 4 to maintain orbital equilibrium."*

a.title: ✕ THAT'S THE SCALE FACTOR, NOT THE ANSWER
body: **4** is the scale factor (`7 × 4 = 28`). That's Step 3 — you're not done yet.
Step 4: apply the same scale factor to the crystals. `5 × 4 = 20 Crystals`.

c.title: ✕ THAT'S ADDITION, NOT SCALING
body: **33** = `5 + 28` — you added the two numbers together. Scaling isn't addition; it's multiplication (or division).
Scale factor is **4** (`7 × 4 = 28`). Then `5 × 4 = 20 Crystals`.

d.title: ✕ TOO MANY CRYSTALS — CHECK THE ROUTINE
body: **140** = `5 × 28`. You multiplied the two numbers directly instead of scaling by the right factor.
The warp routine: find the scale factor from the SAME side first (`7 × ? = 28` → **4**), then multiply the OTHER side by that factor (`5 × 4 = 20`).

wrongDefault.title: ✕ SPACE COMMAND IS STILL WAITING
body: Step 3: **7 × ? = 28**. Lock in that scale factor first.
Step 4: do the same thing to the crystals — 5 × that scale factor.

slides.headline: WARP ROUTINE LOCKED IN
slides.subtext: You can scale any ratio up or down. 5 steps. 2 directions. 1 recipe that stays true. The fleet eats tonight. 🚀
